Ankh Ubiquitination Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: Ankh_ubiquitination_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Embeddings: Ankh • 768-dim  |  Task: binary protein-level ubiquitination classification

1. Dataset

Proteins from UniProt/Swiss-Prot split using the Post-translational modification column:

  • Positive (ubiquitinated): PTM field contains "ubiquitin" (case-insensitive)
  • Negative (not ubiquitinated): PTM field does not mention ubiquitin

2. Methods

2.1 Embeddings

Ankh (768-dim) embeddings, max pooling and attention pooling. All features z-score normalised (training-set statistics only).

2.2 Classifiers

ModelArchitecture / SettingsImbalance handling
Logistic RegressionL2, max_iter=5000class_weight="balanced"
MLP (PyTorch) Linear(768→512)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(512→256)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(256→1), Adam lr=1e-3, 30 epochs, batch=64 BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight=neg/pos

80/20 stratified train/test split, seed 42.

5. Interpretation

5.1 MLP vs Logistic Regression

MLP attn PR-AUC: 0.2891  |  MLP max PR-AUC: 0.2683
LR attn PR-AUC: 0.2237  |  LR max PR-AUC: 0.1909

5.2 Cross-Model Context

Ankh uses 768-dim embeddings. Compare results_ubiquitination_Ankh/, results_ubiquitination_ESM2/, and results_ubiquitination_ProtT5/ for a three-way model comparison on identical data.

5.3 UMAP vs PCA / t-SNE

UMAP preserves global structure better than t-SNE at scale. Substantial overlap between classes is expected for protein-level pooled representations.

5.4 Recommendations

  1. Residue-level classifier on Ankh token embeddings
  2. 5-fold stratified cross-validation instead of single split
  3. Concatenate max + attention pool (2×768) as joint feature
  4. Ensemble Ankh, ESM2 and ProtT5 embeddings
  5. Fine-tune Ankh end-to-end on the ubiquitination task
